content: Success in securing a portion of the substantial public procurement expenditure relies not merely on operational excellence, but on an organizational culture that prioritizes continuous regulatory monitoring, rigorous administrative compliance, and adaptability to the shifting socio-political realities of the South African market. Major Government and SOE Procurement of Security Solutions The global security solutions market exhibited substantial and transformative growth between the years 2020 and 2024, driven by an escalating need to address evolving threat vectors and the rapid pace of technological advancements. During this period, the global security market size demonstrated a consistent upward trajectory, expanding from a baseline value of 105.0 billion USD in 2020 to reach a maximum value of 145.2 billion USD by 2024. This notable expansion underscores a fundamental shift in organizational priorities, as both private enterprises and public institutions increasingly recognized the imperative of investing in robust, comprehensive security infrastructures. The momentum established during these foundational years continued into the subsequent period, with the market reaching an estimated valuation of 156.2 billion USD in 2025, and it is projected to sustain a compound annual growth rate of 6.9 percent through the year 2033 [52] . Major government and state-owned enterprise procurement strategies have been profoundly influenced by these technological shifts and the corresponding regulatory developments. By outlining comprehensive strategies for fostering innovation while ensuring safety and ethical deployment practices, the executive order serves as a critical framework guiding public sector procurement and operational standards [51] . Government and state-owned entities are consequently mandated to align their procurement criteria with these stringent new standards, prioritizing vendors that offer secure, ethically developed, and technologically advanced solutions. However, the rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence, cloud systems, and the Internet of Things has simultaneously expanded the potential attack surface, rendering privacy considerations and advanced defensive measures increasingly pressing [55] .
